promptHead: Athlete goal: marathon (Wexley Lakes Marathon) on Sun Nov 1 2026, 8 weeks out, target under 3:45.

new.headline: This week fell short because of heat, 5.5 hours of sleep and work stress, not lost fitness. Next week holds at 31 mi with a smaller threshold session and an easy 12 mi long run. Don't make up the missed miles.

flags.title: Short week
flags.detail: You missed Thursday, stopped Wednesday after two of three reps and cut Sunday from 13 to 11 mi. That's 27 of 36 planned miles. Don't add them back.

flags.title: Long run ran hard
flags.detail: Sunday averaged a heart rate of 156 with 17% in zone 4, which is a hard effort, not an easy one. Keep this Sunday under 150 and walk when it climbs.

flags.title: Easy heart rate
flags.detail: It jumped from about 139 to 151 while your pace slowed. On Tuesday, check your pace at a heart rate under 145. Close to 10:00/mi means you are bouncing back.

flags.title: Sleep and heat
flags.detail: Sleeping 5.5 hours a night in a hot apartment is the main thing holding you back. Aim for 7 hours, and run before sunrise or indoors until the AC is fixed.

flags.title: Hip and glute work
flags.detail: You did 0 of 2 sessions this week. That work helped settle your right knee in August, so do 15 min after Tuesday's and Thursday's runs.

answers.question: I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?
answers.answer:
No, don't make them up. Missed miles don't carry over. Adding them to a week where you are still sleeping about 5.5 hours in a hot apartment piles fatigue on fatigue. Your right knee also flared up in mid-August, so stacking extra miles while you're tired is a bad trade.

Next week totals 31 mi, with a 12 mi long run, one mile more than Sunday. That starts from where your body is now, not where the plan said you'd be. Once your sleep and the heat improve, the long run starts growing again.

new.analysis:
**Heat, short sleep and a work deadline explain this week, not lost fitness.** Your easy pace slowed and your heart rate rose at the same time, which is what heat and poor sleep do. In early August, in cooler weather, the same kinds of runs looked very different.

| | Early August | This week |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy run pace | 9:50/mi | 10:28/mi |
| Easy run heart rate | 139 | 151 |
| Long run pace | 10:00/mi | about 10:35/mi while moving |
| Long run heart rate | 146 | 156 |

**Stopping Wednesday after two reps was the right call.** The reps came in at 8:18/mi against the planned 8:00/mi, and they felt like 9/10. A third rep in that heat would have cost more recovery than it built.

**Sunday was harder on you than planned.** An average heart rate of 156 makes it closer to a steady run than an easy long run. Cutting it at 11 mi was sensible, and that effort is part of why you feel drained.

**Only 11% of your running was easy, and that was the heat, not your choices.** Even your easy runs drifted into zone 3, so pace targets stopped working. Until it cools down, run by heart rate and accept the slower pace that comes with it.

**Next week holds steady rather than building because recovery is what's limiting you.** Sleep, heat and the deadline are already draining you, and hard training drains the same reserves. So the volume stays close to your early-August weeks. The threshold work gets smaller instead of disappearing, and the long run grows by only a mile.

**The long run is where the next five weeks need to go.** Eight weeks out, your longest run is 12 mi, which is behind where I'd like it. Once you are sleeping well and the heat breaks, it should grow 1 to 2 mi a week. The aim is 18 to 20 mi by early October, with a lighter week along the way. One easy run during the week will also stretch to 7 or 8 mi.

**Under 3:45 is still within reach.** In cool weather your threshold reps at 8:00/mi felt like 7/10, and goal pace is 8:35/mi. The open question is whether you can hold that pace for the whole distance. Longer long runs, with marathon-pace sections later on, will answer it.

settingsProposalBullets: The outside of your right knee hurt on the Aug 16 long run, sharp on downhills, and settled within a week with daily hip and glute work.
In cool weather your easy runs sit around 9:50/mi at a heart rate of 138 to 140, and your threshold reps around 8:00/mi.
You do two short hip and glute sessions a week, after your Tuesday and Thursday easy runs.

safetyCallouts.title: Know the signs of heat trouble.
safetyCallouts.body: If you feel dizzy, sick or confused, get chills or stop sweating, stop running, get into shade, cool down and drink. Get medical help if it does not settle quickly.

safetyCallouts.title: Tiredness that will not lift.
safetyCallouts.body: If you still feel drained and your easy heart rate stays high a week after the AC is fixed and you are sleeping 7 hours, see your doctor before training harder.
